entry.label: Requisite inefficiency
entry.description: The proposal that some slack, redundancy or apparently unused variety is necessary if a system is to retain the capacity to respond and remain viable under conditions not already anticipated.
entry.canonical_definition: The proposal that some slack, redundancy or apparently unused variety is necessary if a system is to retain the capacity to respond and remain viable under conditions not already anticipated.

profile.title: Requisite inefficiency
profile.canonical_definition: The proposal that some slack, redundancy or apparently unused variety is necessary if a system is to retain the capacity to respond and remain viable under conditions not already anticipated.
profile.summary: Requisite inefficiency names the possibility that unused capacity, redundancy, variation or slack may be regulatory resource rather than waste.
profile.why_it_matters: Efficiency programmes can remove the very variety needed to absorb disturbance, learn, experiment and respond. The concept forces an explicit question: inefficient relative to which purpose, boundary and timescale?
key_distinctions: efficiency for one part vs capacity of the whole
open_checks: distinguish related concepts such as slack, redundancy and reserve variety
profile.editorial_note: Developed from cited public sources. The entry remains open to correction, rival accounts and stronger evidence.
